name: The Camp
reads: Tents, a picket line and a standard planted in the ground. Everything you have is portable, because until now everything has had to be.
disputed: A generic pre-royal camp. Nothing about Cyrus' encampments is recorded.

name: The Watered Garden
reads: Straight stone channels carrying water across a dry plain, and planting laid out along them. The Greeks borrowed a Persian word for this and we still use it: paradise.

name: The Audience Hall
reads: A columned hall standing on its own in the garden rather than inside a fortress wall. A king who builds without walls is saying something about how safe he feels.

name: The Gatehouse
reads: A doorway with a winged figure carved beside it, wearing an Egyptian crown, Elamite dress and Assyrian wings. Whoever it is, it is not one thing.
disputed: Who the winged figure represents — Cyrus, a guardian spirit, or something else — has been argued for two centuries and is not settled.

name: The Tomb
reads: A plain gabled chamber on a stepped plinth, standing by itself on the plain. It is still there.
disputed: The inscription Greek writers report on it is not preserved, and its wording comes to us only through them.
